title: DENR encourages cycling for cleaner air
summary: The Department of Environment and Natural Resources on Sunday encouraged the public to consider using a bicycle as an alternative mode of transportation to address air pollution in the country.

blocks.text: The Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) on Sunday encouraged the public to consider using a bicycle as an alternative mode of transportation to address air pollution in the country.
The department also highly suggested to the public to consider walking or riding a bicycle for short trips.

“As I have always said, everyone can help fight climate change. When we rethink our ways of travelling, when we walk or ride a bike instead of driving, we become part of the solution to the climate crisis,” said DENR Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna in a statement.
The National Bicycle Day, which is observed every fourth Sunday of November under Proclamation No. 1052, falls on November 22 this year.
The DENR also launched the Bike-to-Work Campaign for its personnel, which encourages department employees to get into cycling.

"The Department's campaign seeks to encourage sustained cycling among its workforce beyond the annual celebration. The initiative, undertaken in partnership with the Environmental Management Bureau (EMB) and the DoTr Active Transport Project Office (ATPO), aims to promote active mobility, reduce dependence on motorized transportation, and contribute to cleaner air and lower greenhouse gas emissions," the DENR said.
"It will also feature a GHG (Greenhouse Gases) Calculator that will help employees estimate benefits of their work-related bicycle commutes," it added.
There are concentrations of particulate matter (PM) 2.5 in the air, according to the Manila Observatory.

The common sources of PM 2.5 pollution in Metro Manila are motor vehicle exhaust, construction site dust, road dust, practices related to waste management, and the burning of organic matter, known as biomass burning. Contributions also come from natural sources, such as sea salt. —Vince Angelo Ferreras/KG, GMA News
